title: Propagating context through the whole call: the first-parameter convention

videos.script: Lesson 10 made a context and cancelled it inside one function. Real programs are many functions deep. This lesson carries one context from the top of a request to the bottom. {{layers}} First, the convention. The context is the first parameter, it is called ctx, and every function that can wait takes it. You watch three layers. The top sets a deadline. The middle only passes it on. The bottom stops when it runs out. {{tree}} Then the tree. A child context can be shorter than its parent, never longer. Cancelling a child leaves its parent alone. An ending flows down, never up. {{edges}} Two tools sit at the edges. One runs cleanup when a request ends. The other lets a small piece of work outlive it. {{loop}} Last, the part people forget. A context stops nothing by itself. Two loops get the same deadline. One looks at it and stops on time. The other never looks, and runs seven times too long. {{close}} Lesson 12 puts all of this into a server.
